name: Xàtiva (Spain)
description: Red field charged at the centre with a lozenge of the bars of Aragon beneath a yellow crown.
history: The flag or senyera of Xàtiva is the traditional symbol representing the royal standard on a red field, granted to the city by King Peter the Ceremonious in 1347 for its loyalty to the king during the War of the Union, when he rewarded it by declaring it a city and granting the privilege of bearing the royal standard on a red field. All the towns and places of its general territory were obliged in case of war to supply men to form militias under the flag of Xàtiva. The oldest graphic representation of the senyera is on a Baroque ceramic tile altarpiece on the façade of the Casa Artigues near the bell tower of the Seu; the flag is very popular in the city and flies from the castle and many monumental buildings.

features.role: lozenge of the four red bars of Aragon
